newsitem.title: UK: Adverts target kids with junk food, study finds.
newsitem.headline: Adverts target kids with junk food, study finds.

text.p: Advertisers are targeting children with television commercials featuring high-fat, sugary and salty foods, an international consumers' group said on Monday.
Consumers International said a survey it conducted found more than half of all food advertisements on television in 13 countries were for fast-food restaurants, sweets and breakfast cereals.

"Most governments and the World Health Organisation are trying to promote the importance of healthy, balanced diets, especially for children," Lucy Harris, of Consumers International, said in a statement.
"This report shows that TV food advertising essentially undermines that message."

The organisation, which includes 215 consumer groups in more than 90 countries, surveyed television advertising in Australia, Austria, Britain, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United States.

It found British television showed the most advertising during children's programming with an average of 17 commercials an hour, 10 of which were for food. Ninety-five percent of the advertised foods contained high amounts of fat, sugar or salt.

Australia had the most television food advertising directed at children, with an average of 12 food commercials an hour. Sweden and Norway, where a virtual ban exists on television advertising aimed at children, had the least.
The most prolific advertiser during children's programmes was fast-food giant McDonald's.

"The choice that food advertising presents children is largely one between one candy bar and another, the latest savoury snack or sweetened breakfast cereal or fast-food restaurant -- hardly the kind of choices which encourage a healthy balanced diet," Consumers International said.
It called for more restrictions on advertising to children as well as clearer breaks between programmes and commercials.
